subject: Music Production
title: The Speed of Sound
description: A fast breakdown of The Speed of Sound for builders.

hook.text: You see lightning instantly but hear the thunder seconds later because sound travels slowly.

buildup.text: Sound moves through air at about three hundred forty-three meters per second at room temperature.

discovery.text: The speed of sound changes with temperature, humidity, and the density of the material it moves through.

twist.text: Sound travels four times faster through water and fifteen times faster through steel than air.

climax.text: Producers account for sound speed when placing microphones to avoid phase issues in recordings.

punchline.text: Sound is fast, but light still beats it every time.

quiz.question: Through which medium does sound travel fastest?
